name: Tetralogy of Fallot in Adults

prevalence.estimate: 1 in 3,000 live births (congenital), adult prevalence lower due to childhood repair

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Echocardiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Tetralogy of Fallot

criteria.description: Presence of a large, non-restrictive ventricular septal defect
Right ventricular outflow tract obstruction or pulmonary stenosis
Aortic root overriding the ventricular septal defect
Right ventricular hypertrophy evident on imaging or ECG
Clinical evidence of cyanosis or hypoxemia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all four major anatomical abnormalities (VSD, pulmonary stenosis, overriding aorta, right ventricular hypertrophy) confirmed by imaging or surgical history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis in adults often relies on history of childhood repair and current imaging findings due to variable presentation.

pathognomonic.notes: Bluish discoloration of lips and mucous membranes due to hypoxemia
Digital clubbing secondary to chronic hypoxia

common.notes: Shortness of breath on physical activity
Generalized tiredness related to reduced cardiac output
Systolic murmur due to right ventricular outflow obstruction
Arrhythmias common in repaired or unrepaired TOF

occasional.notes: Transient loss of consciousness due to arrhythmia or hypoxia
May occur due to myocardial ischemia or arrhythmias
Coughing up blood, rare but possible due to collateral vessels

rare.notes: Due to paradoxical embolism or septic emboli
Infection of cardiac valves or patches
Fatal arrhythmias in unrepaired or residual defects
searchTerms: unexpected cardiac arrest from rhythm problems

imaging: Echocardiography showing VSD, overriding aorta, RV hypertrophy, and pulmonary stenosis
Cardiac MRI for detailed anatomy and function
genetic: No single gene mutation; associated with 22q11.2 deletion syndrome in some cases
other: Electrocardiogram showing right ventricular hypertrophy and right axis deviation

distinguishingFeatures: Aorta arises from right ventricle, pulmonary artery from left ventricle

redFlags: Signs of right heart failure or arrhythmia
references: Gatzoulis MA, Balaji S, Webber SA, et al. Risk factors for arrhythmia and sudden cardiac death late after repair of tetralogy of Fallot: a multicenter study. Circulation. 2000;102(20): 2329-2335.
Warnes CA, Liberthson R, Danielson GK, et al. ACC/AHA 2008 Guidelines for the Management of Adults with Congenital Heart Disease. Circulation. 2008;118(23):e714-e833.
Baumgartner H, Bonhoeffer P, De Groot NM, et al. ESC Guidelines for the management of grown-up congenital heart disease. Eur Heart J. 2010;31(23):2915-2957.
